approachQuestion.prompt:
Storage Bins

Rearrange a mutable array codes so that every even integer appears before every odd integer. The relative order within either group is irrelevant. Return b, the number of even entries, with codes[0:b] all even and codes[b:n] all odd. Preserve all entries and do not resize the array.

Constraints: 0 <= n = codes.length <= 200000; 0 <= codes[i] <= 1000000000.

Example 1: codes = [3,2,7,4,8] -> b = 3; one valid array is [8,2,4,7,3].
Example 2: codes = [1,5] -> b = 0; [1,5] is valid.
Example 3: codes = [] -> b = 0.
constraints: Choose the most efficient valid approach for the entire stated input domain; accept equivalent optimal variants.

options.text: Advance a left index over even entries and a right index over odd entries. When left < right, swap those misplaced entries and advance both. Return the left index after the indices cross.
options.feedback: The passed left prefix is even and the passed right suffix is odd. A swap fixes one entry on each side; stability is not required.

options.text: Scan left to right with a boundary b starting at zero. Whenever the current entry is even, swap it with codes[b] and increment b. Return b.
options.feedback: The prefix before b always contains the even entries seen so far; the scan handles every entry once.

options.text: Collect even entries and odd entries into two arrays, copy them back consecutively, and return the even count.
options.feedback: This is correct, but the temporary arrays are unnecessary because arbitrary within-group order is allowed.

options.text: Count even entries and return that count without changing codes.
options.feedback: For [1,2], returning 1 leaves an odd entry in the required even prefix.

feedback.reason: Partition an unsorted sequence by a predicate while distinguishing permitted swaps from a stable-order requirement.
details: Use left=0 and right=n-1. Skip even entries from the left and odd entries from the right while left<=right. If left<right, swap the two misplaced entries and move both inward. Stop when left>right and return left.

Entries outside the active interval are already on the correct parity side. Swap only the two misplaced entries found by inward scans; the final left boundary separates the partitions even when one side is empty.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method revealed after question 1, choose its tight worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Use a word-RAM model with constant-time indexed access and signed 64-bit arithmetic. Include all temporary buffers, input copies, and call frames; exclude supplied input and returned output. Here n is the original array length. The iterative method uses no recursion, hashing, copies, or amortized container operations.
constraints: Analyze this fixed method regardless of your answer to question 1; choose the tightest pair.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(1) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Each index crosses the input once, with one swap temporary.
details: Each index crosses at most n positions; the scans and swaps together do linear work in the worst case, including an all-even input. Only indices and a swap temporary are needed.

Use a word-RAM model with constant-time indexed access and signed 64-bit arithmetic. Include all temporary buffers, input copies, and call frames; exclude supplied input and returned output. Here n is the original array length. The iterative method uses no recursion, hashing, copies, or amortized container operations.
“O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: This adds an input-sized buffer absent from the fixed method.
“O(n²) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: This counts repeated full scans that the fixed method does not perform.
“O(n log n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The fixed method does not perform sorting or independent binary searches.
